Hi Dung, I've taken a quick look and from what I can see there are a few issues that are covered in the changes checklist:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md#adding-a-new-api

Do you mind working your way through that and reworking the patch accordingly?

Hi Andrew,I changed a little bit on the function name, enum, and struct. 
Please comment if anything I need to do more.
Hi Dung, thanks for the rework so far. I've highlighted a few more areas where changes are required.
Can we please have consistency between the type and member names? Either use `_xfer_` here or `_TRANSFER_` in the member names.
Done. Updated to `TRANSFER`.
Where's this used? It's not used by either of the function prototypes below, which appears to go against https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L126-L127

Done. Replaced by `pldm_multipart_receive_resp`. However, I do not include the DataIntegrityChecksum field to the struct, because of the flexible array on top of it. I separate it to another output argument that callers need to pass into the decode function.
See https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L117-L123
Done

Please not for new APIs. See https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L168-L169

Also, something I've been considering that I'd like to experiment with here is requiring that `encode_*()` functions return `ssize_t`, with `-1` on error, and the size of the payload buffer consumed by the encoding on success.
I updated the description. But I don't quite understand your experiment suggestion. Do you mean that I should return with the total bytes of `buf` that are already extracted to the output params?
See https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L117-L123
Updated, please help me review new argument declaration.
See https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L168-L169
Updated, please help me review new description.

Before the `pldm_msgbuf_init_errno()` call below, I think we need a call to `pldm_msg_has_error()` (from `src/dsp/base.h`). That way we cater to error responses before requiring the minimum buffer size be the expected response length.
Done

Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, thank you a lot for your thorough review and sorry for late response. I have alr addressed your comments below. Can you please help see if they match current expectation of libpldm.
Hi Chau, I've left some further comments inline. Thanks for reworking it so far.
Thank you.

Must we expose this in the public header? I realise others are, but I'd really prefer we don't if it's not necessary.

Eventually I'd like to remove the others.

Please move it to the implementation if it's not intended to be used by a library user.
Actually, disregard this, it was a thoughtless comment that I shouldn't have made. My apologies.
ACK.

My (current) preference is we use a `struct variable_field` here, and populate it with `pldm_msgbuf_span_remaining()` in the decode implementation.

The flexible array doesn't make sense for decoding purposes if the struct can't be cast over the buffer (which it can't, because it's not packed, and we don't want it to be).
Updated. But I chose to use `pldm_msgbuf_span_required()` as we might still have the checksum part at the end of the buffer, so we rely on the `length` field to extract the data.
Please be complete with the documentation, avoid catch all phrases like this one at the end.
Done
The formatting here looks broken. Can you please fix it?
Done
Hmm, I'll mull this one over for a bit.
I think I'm fine with this.
If we don't use a flexible array in the struct then this is unnecessary.
Done

I recommend avoiding the `_consumed()` variant here, as we want to allow the caller to pass in larger buffers than required without causing an error. If we make `payload_length` a in-out pointer parameter then we can instead pass back out the encoded message size using `pldm_msgbuf_destroy_used()`.
Updated to use `pldm_msgbuf_destroy()`

Please avoid using the `_p()` variants in new code. Instead use `pldm_msgbuf_extract(buf, resp->completion_code)`

Fix this throughout.

Done. But I still use `pldm_msgbuf_extract_p(buf, data_integrity_checksum);`, otherwise it will throw `error: pointer parameter 'data_integrity_checksum' can be pointer to const [readability-non-const-parameter,-warnings-as-errors]` during clang-tidy. Will proceed after you give more feedback about `data_integrity_checksum`.
This is already tested by `pldm_msg_has_error()` above.
Done
This is already tested by `pldm_msgbuf_init_errno()` above.
Done
Need to test the result of this because you use `resp->transfer_flag` below.
Done

Rather, just use `ASSERT_NE(respData, nullptr);` and avoid the `if (respData)`. But that goes away by dropping the flexible array as mentioned in my comment on the header.

Look for other opportunities to use `ASSERT_*()` macros throughout.
Done

This shouldn't be a pointer, rather a proper `struct variable field` object. Just populate the `ptr` member with the pointer into the message buffer, and then populate the `length` member appropriately.

Acknowledged. Please help review my edit. At first I removed the `uint32_t data_length;` field to avoid duplication with the `length` field in the variable_field struct. But `pldm_msgbuf_extract` does not work with `size_t` so it needs casting and breaks the macro with `error: lvalue required as unary ‘&’ operand`, which led me to directly using `pldm__msgbuf_extract_uint32`. I think this is not good, so now I define a local uint32_t var to hold the data length from extraction and assign it back to `length` for use. Both ways seem to make the function be aware of the data type of data length (an element of the struct), I don't know if I should put data_length back to the struct.

Are you interested in working on adding e.g. a `pldm_msgbuf_extract_uint32_size()` API? I was also considering that recently after hitting similar limitations with the existing msgbuf APIs. I think that would make the code more ergonomic.

> #define pldm_msgbuf_extract_uint32_size(ctx, dst)                                   \
	pldm__msgbuf_extract_uint32(ctx, (void *)&(dst))
	
Do you mean the above? I think it still requires the encode/decode API to know beforehand about the type of an element in the struct, which can possibly be changed after spec update.

I can try it. How should I easily apply changes upon your existing patches without having to update them every time you push new changes? Btw, I can't find the command to quickly cherry-pick the whole relation chain, do you have any suggestion? Thanks.

Great!

I read through your patches and see no flaw in them initially. I will try to see more carefully.

I added a patch in front of this patch to support pldm_msgbuf_extract_uint*_to_size (). I tested them upon your patches. But I did not rebase on your patches here, it has no compiling dependency so it still passes. I also updated this patch to use `pldm_msgbuf_extract_uint32_to_size()` and the patch https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/78851 to use `pldm_msgbuf_extract_uint8_to_size()`.

ACK. But I also constructed an array to be compared with the requestMsg at the end, just like what was done for EncodeDfOpenReq as you suggested here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/78996/comment/8548b45a_f57cb2cb/

`ASSERT_EQ(pldm_msgbuf_complete*(), 0);` must come _before_ the call into the `encode_*()` or `decode_*()` libpldm APIs, otherwise your test might be invalid. That is, this should be placed somewhere after line 926 and before line 930.
